points.description: States that a (near) zero voltage reading across a part/bulb means there is no gap (the connection is complete, so that part is not the break); a non-zero/high (e.g. full supply) voltage across a component indicates the gap/break is there, i.e. the burned-out bulb. Accept equivalent wording: zero voltage = no gap/complete connection. Vague answers without reference to voltage and a gap/connection earn no marks.

rubric.notes: Full mark for linking zero voltage to no gap (or equivalently, a voltage across a component to a gap/break at the burned-out bulb). No marks for answers that do not link voltage to gap/connection.
